newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska soy harvest 98 pct complete, corn 45 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska soy harvest 98 pct complete, corn 45 pct.

text.p: Soybean harvest was nearly complete while corn combining was nearing the halfway mark in the week ended Sunday, according to the weekly crop report from the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
Soybeans were 98 percent harvested as of Sunday, compared with the five-year average of 94 percent. Corn was 45 percent combined, trailing the average of 57 percent.
Sorghum harvest was 28 percent complete, about 18 days behind the average of 66 percent.
"Sorghum harvest continued to be delayed due to high moisture levels and wet field conditions," the report said.
"Winds in excess of 50 miles per hour were recorded on Saturday, causing some lodging of corn and sorghum," it said.
Emergence of winter wheat was 97 percent complete, against a 98 percent average. The crop was rated three percent poor, 27 percent fair, 60 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
Pasture and range were rated three percent poor, 17 percent fair, 70 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
Soil moisture was rated two percent very short, 21 percent short, 75 percent adequate and two percent surplus.
